thesis: Yesterday's energy thesis got one genuinely new fact behind it rather than just a favorable tape. The IEA now says a Strait of Hormuz blockade is driving up global coal use, which is an institutional confirmation that the disruption is physical and is already forcing fuel substitution, and crude has traded back above 100 dollars as the Iran war escalates further. A blockade confirmed by the energy agency is exactly the durable supply fact I said in June I would require before treating energy as more than a headline, and it is a different kind of evidence from the price move itself. So I add to XOM, but only 3 dollars, and the size is the honest part of this batch. I am nearly fully invested: cash is about 9.4% of equity against a 5% floor, and a 3 dollar add leaves roughly 7%, which still holds the floor even if my positions opened sharply higher. A larger add would have to be funded by selling tech, and I am not doing that today. The same headline says stocks are falling on Wall Street, and selling my long-duration sleeves into that print would be trading the tape, which I refused when futures were rising on 6/9 and again when they were falling on 9/8. I also want to name the risk in my own behavior: escalation has now driven three consecutive decisions, and if each day's confirmation justifies a bigger energy weight, that is a momentum trade dressed as a thesis. Keeping the add small is how I stay on the right side of that line. XOM goes to roughly 12% of equity, which is a real position but not a bet the book depends on. Nothing else in the pack is actionable for me. Intel possibly raising prices again is interesting for semiconductor pricing but Intel is not in my 20 symbols and the read-through to NVDA is my inference, not the pack's. Delek rallying and Bloom Energy's index addition are outside the universe, Michael Burry's view on Palantir is opinion about a name I cannot trade, and 'if a stock market crash is coming, buy this growth stock' is clickbait. After fills the book holds 4 of 8 positions, NVDA stays near 39% inside the 50% cap, and cash sits above the floor.
